scenarios.requirement: A language with no error-message pattern does not read past memory when F9 reports errors
A pattern that ends inside a test does not read past memory when F9 reports errors
A pattern with fewer rows than the maximum does not read past memory when F9 reports errors
Every message pattern of a compiler the editor knows is read with its rows, warning tests and file naming, and a pattern literal added to the editor without being added to the unit's list fails
scenarios.note: pass A, compile half; red when the row splitter is stubbed off

scenarios.requirement: A pattern cut inside a ${...} token, a [...] class or a backslash, an empty pattern and one with no ${LINE} are refused with a reason naming the token; an unknown variable, rows past the fourth and a non-numeric warning column are accepted with a note
scenarios.note: pass A; red when R1, R2, R3, R4 or R8 is stubbed off (measured on scratch copies of we_errpat.c)

scenarios.requirement: A '$' that is not followed by '{' is an ordinary byte, and the classes and escapes the matcher reads today are accepted unchanged
scenarios.note: the golden table rows for classes, escapes and a lone dollar cover the match half

scenarios.requirement: Reading and walking any pattern built from the fuzz tokens (seeds 0 to 3999) ends, reads nothing outside the text or a row, makes no more entries than there are rows, and gives the same answer twice; the same seeds go through the matcher unchecked
scenarios.note: compile half and walk half; the unchecked pass bypasses compile

scenarios.requirement: Every row of the golden table gives the same entries as the matcher the editor had before the pattern had an owner: file, line, column, kind, whether it stops the build, the rows it names and the last row it uses
scenarios.note: pass B; the table is measured on f2305d3

scenarios.requirement: A walk always moves on and stays inside the rows, and a pattern that backtracks without end costs one row that does not match
scenarios.note: pass B; red on f2305d3 where the walk gave a row back past its start

scenarios.requirement: A warning test at a column past the end of a row never reads past the row
scenarios.note: pass B; the row is a block of exactly its size, red under the sanitizer on f2305d3

scenarios.requirement: F9 ends with its count line when a two-row pattern's first row is the last row of Messages
scenarios.note: pass B; red on f2305d3: F9 stays on building

scenarios.requirement: A build whose last rows end in a backslash is read to its end inside Messages
scenarios.note: pass B; red under the sanitizer on f2305d3

scenarios.requirement: A pattern that ends inside a warning test ${?*:text} ends the build with its count line and one Messages row naming the cut
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: no row says why

scenarios.requirement: A pattern row that ends in a backslash ends the build with its count line and one Messages row saying the pattern was not used
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: no row says why

scenarios.requirement: A row that costs the pattern more steps than the budget is left unrecognised and one Messages row names it
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: the row is dropped without a word

scenarios.requirement: With the GNU style the row that names a costly pattern row names the built-in GNU pattern and says how to use one's own, not the language's MessageString
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: no row; red on the build that names the MessageString whatever the style

scenarios.requirement: Two builds in one session each end with the pattern row
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: no row; red on the build that never clears the said flag

scenarios.requirement: A pattern with an unknown variable is used, and one Messages row says the variable was read as *
scenarios.note: pass C; red on 0416b27: the note is never shown
